1	# 24_herdr.sh - herdr workspace layout helpers (shared backend; bash 4+ / zsh).
2	# https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr
3	#
4	# herdr-native analogs of the sesh/tmux helpers in 22_sesh.sh. herdr's model is
5	# Workspace -> Tab -> Pane (tmux is Session -> Window -> Pane), and its CLI
6	# (`herdr workspace|tab|pane|agent …`) is the scripting surface that replaces
7	# `tmux new-session/split-window`.
8	#
9	# Backend that powers the user-facing commands and their aliases:
10	#   herdr-vibe / hvibe  — parametric multi-agent pack in a new workspace
11	#                         (N agent panes + lazygit tab + nvim tab)
12	#   herdr-code / hcode  — repo-scoped single-agent layout
13	#                         (nvim | agent split + btop monitor tab)
14	#
15	# REUSE: the *pure* (multiplexer-agnostic) helpers from 22_sesh.sh are reused
16	# verbatim — `_sesh_git_root`, `_sesh_sanitize`, `_sesh_wrap_agent` (specstory
17	# wrapping), `_sesh_on_exit_wrap` (shell|kill|restart post-exit behavior).
18	# 22_sesh.sh sorts before this file, so they are defined by the time hvibe/hcode
19	# run. Only the tmux calls are swapped for `herdr …` CLI calls.
20	#
21	# Bash baseline: 4+ (same array-slicing idiom as svibe; no `local -A`).
22	
23	# Skip entirely if herdr isn't installed (it's a trial tool, not on every host).
24	command -v herdr >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
25	
26	# ── Internal helpers ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
27	
28	# Echo the workspace_id of an existing workspace whose label == $1 (else empty).
29	# Used for idempotency: re-running hvibe/hcode in a repo focuses the existing
30	# workspace instead of stacking duplicates (mirrors svibe's has-session check).
31	function _herdr_ws_by_label() {
32	    herdr workspace list 2>/dev/null \
33	        | jq -r --arg l "$1" '.result.workspaces[]? | select(.label==$l) | .workspace_id' 2>/dev/null \
34	        | head -1
35	}
36	
37	# Compose the shell command for one agent pane: specstory-wrap then on-exit-wrap.
38	# $1=agent  $2=specstory_mode(auto|never)  $3=on_exit(shell|kill|restart)
39	function _herdr_agent_cmd() {
40	    local inner
41	    inner=$(_sesh_wrap_agent "$1" "$2")
42	    _sesh_on_exit_wrap "$inner" "$3" "${1:-agent}"
43	}
44	
45	# Create a labeled tab in workspace $1 (cwd $2, label $3) and run command $4 in
46	# its root pane. `tab create` returns the new pane id at .result.root_pane.
47	# $1=workspace_id  $2=cwd  $3=label  $4=command
48	function _herdr_tool_tab() {
49	    local pane
50	    pane=$(herdr tab create --workspace "$1" --cwd "$2" --label "$3" --no-focus 2>/dev/null \
51	        | jq -r '.result.root_pane.pane_id // empty')
52	    [ -n "$pane" ] && herdr pane run "$pane" "$4" >/dev/null 2>&1
53	}
54	
55	# Resolve the target herdr session for hvibe/hcode from an optional --session
56	# value. Echoes "<name><TAB><socket_override_or_empty>". The socket field is
57	# non-empty ONLY when the caller must override HERDR_SOCKET_PATH (explicit
58	# --session); empty means "use the ambient/default socket untouched". Returns 1
59	# (with a message) when an explicit --session names a session that isn't running.
60	#
61	# A herdr server hosts multiple named sessions (default + `herdr --session NAME`),
62	# each with its own socket. The CLI has no --session flag on subcommands; the
63	# only lever is the HERDR_SOCKET_PATH env var (verified). `session list --json`
64	# is the authoritative name -> socket_path resolver.
65	function _herdr_session_target() {
66	    local want="$1" js line running socket nm
67	    js=$(herdr session list --json 2>/dev/null)
68	    if [ -n "$want" ]; then
69	        line=$(printf '%s' "$js" \
70	            | jq -r --arg n "$want" '.sessions[] | select(.name==$n) | "\(.running)\t\(.socket_path)"' 2>/dev/null \
71	            | head -1)
72	        if [ -z "$line" ]; then
73	            echo "session '$want' not found. Start it with: herdr --session $want" >&2
74	            return 1
75	        fi
76	        running=${line%%$'\t'*}
77	        socket=${line#*$'\t'}
78	        if [ "$running" != "true" ]; then
79	            echo "session '$want' is not running. Start it with: herdr --session $want" >&2
80	            return 1
81	        fi
82	        printf '%s\t%s\n' "$want" "$socket"
83	        return 0
84	    fi
85	    # No explicit --session: inside herdr use the ambient session (no override);
86	    # outside, fall back to the default session. Only the NAME matters here (for
87	    # the attach path) — socket stays empty so the ambient socket is left as-is.
88	    if [ -n "$HERDR_SOCKET_PATH" ]; then
89	        nm=$(printf '%s' "$js" \
90	            | jq -r --arg s "$HERDR_SOCKET_PATH" '.sessions[] | select(.socket_path==$s) | .name' 2>/dev/null \
91	            | head -1)
92	        printf '%s\t\n' "${nm:-default}"
93	    else
94	        printf 'default\t\n'
95	    fi
96	}

98	# When hvibe/hcode run from OUTSIDE herdr, bring up a client attached to the
99	# session so the just-created/focused workspace is actually visible — the
100	# `herdr workspace focus` calls only move an ALREADY-attached client. Inside
101	# herdr (HERDR_ENV set) those focus calls already switched the live client, so
102	# there is nothing to do. Runs the client as a child (no exec), mirroring
103	# svibe's `tmux attach-session`. $1=session_name (default: "default").
104	function _herdr_attach_if_outside() {
105	    [ -n "$HERDR_ENV" ] && return 0
106	    local session="${1:-default}"
107	    if [ "$session" = "default" ]; then
108	        herdr
109	    else
110	        herdr session attach "$session"
111	    fi
112	}

114	# ── hvibe: parametric multi-agent pack ──────────────────────────────────────
115	#
116	# A herdr "vibe" workspace: tab "agents" with N agent panes (side-by-side
117	# splits by default), tab "git" (lazygit), tab "edit" (nvim). Built directly
118	# with herdr CLI calls so pane count stays parametric.
119	#
120	# Workspace label: `vibe/<repo-basename>` (idempotent — re-running focuses it).
121	# Refuses outside a git repo (pass -p DIR, or cd into a repo).
122	#
123	# Each agent pane is specstory-wrapped (known providers) and on-exit-wrapped,
124	# exactly like `svibe` — the wrapping helpers are shared, only the layout calls
125	# differ. herdr auto-detects agent state per pane, so all N agents surface
126	# individually in the sidebar even when they share the "agents" tab.
127	#
128	# Two modes for choosing agents (same as svibe):
129	#   Homogeneous (positional):  hvibe 3 codex        → 3 panes all codex
130	#   Heterogeneous (--agents):  hvibe --agents claude,codex,opencode
131	#
132	# --tab-per-agent puts each agent in its OWN tab (own rolled-up state dot in the
133	# sidebar) instead of side-by-side splits — better for many agents, since herdr
134	# has no even-out-splits command.
135	#
136	# Usage:
137	#   hvibe                                       # auto N × claude (specstory)
138	#   hvibe 2                                     # 2× claude
139	#   hvibe 3 codex                               # 3× specstory run codex
140	#   hvibe 2 opencode                            # 2× opencode (raw)
141	#   hvibe --agents claude,codex,opencode        # 3 panes, mixed
142	#   hvibe --tab-per-agent --agents claude,codex # one tab each
143	#   hvibe --no-specstory 2 claude               # raw claude, no md auto-save
144	#   hvibe --on-exit restart 2 codex             # auto-respawn loop
145	#   hvibe -p ~/repo 2 claude                    # explicit path
146	#   hvibe --no-attach 2 claude                  # create in background
147	function herdr-vibe() {
148	    command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "hvibe: jq is required." >&2; return 1; }
149	
150	    local target="" no_attach=0 on_exit="shell" specstory_mode="auto" session_arg=""
151	    local n_agents=0 n_agents_set=0 agent_cli="claude" agents_csv="" tab_per_agent=0
152	    local min_width="${HVIBE_MIN_WIDTH:-80}"
153	    # Stagger between pane launches so agents that share a global resource at
154	    # cold start (opencode's single SQLite DB + WAL pragma) don't race. Set 0
155	    # to launch all at once. Same rationale as svibe's SVIBE_LAUNCH_STAGGER.
156	    local launch_stagger="${HVIBE_LAUNCH_STAGGER:-0.25}"
157	
158	    while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
159	        case "$1" in
160	            -p|--path)       target="$2"; shift 2 ;;
161	            --on-exit)       on_exit="$2"; shift 2 ;;
162	            --agents)        agents_csv="$2"; shift 2 ;;
163	            --session)       session_arg="$2"; shift 2 ;;
164	            --min-width)     min_width="$2"; shift 2 ;;
165	            --tab-per-agent) tab_per_agent=1; shift ;;
166	            --no-specstory)  specstory_mode="never"; shift ;;
167	            --specstory)     specstory_mode="auto"; shift ;;
168	            --no-attach)     no_attach=1; shift ;;
169	            -h|--help)
170	                cat <<'EOF'
171	hvibe — herdr multi-agent pack (herdr analog of svibe)
172	
173	Usage:
174	  hvibe [--path DIR] [--on-exit MODE] [--no-specstory] [--no-attach]
175	        [--min-width COLS] [--tab-per-agent] [--session NAME] [N_AGENTS] [AGENT_CLI]
176	  hvibe [--path DIR] [--on-exit MODE] [--no-specstory] [--no-attach]
177	        [--min-width COLS] [--tab-per-agent] [--session NAME] --agents A1,A2,A3[,...]
178	
179	Builds a new herdr workspace `vibe/<repo>`:
180	  tab "agents" — N agent panes (side-by-side splits; each auto-detected in
181	                 the sidebar). --tab-per-agent → one tab per agent instead.
182	  tab "git"    — lazygit (falls back to `git status`)
183	  tab "edit"   — nvim
184	Idempotent: re-running in the same repo focuses the existing workspace.
185	Requires:  a git repo (pass -p DIR, or cd into one).
186	
187	Attach behavior: run from OUTSIDE herdr → attaches a client to the session so

189	--no-attach builds in the background either way.
190	--session NAME targets a running herdr session (default: the current session

193	
194	Two modes for choosing agents:
195	  Homogeneous:    hvibe 3 codex → 3 panes all codex
196	  Heterogeneous:  hvibe --agents claude,codex,opencode  (list length = panes)
197	
198	Agent wrapping (auto, opt out with --no-specstory):

200	  opencode (and other unknown CLIs)         → raw passthrough
201	
202	--on-exit MODE (per pane, on Ctrl+C / clean exit):
203	  shell (default) — drop to a shell with a re-run hint
204	  kill            — let the pane close
205	  restart         — auto-respawn in a loop
206	
207	--min-width COLS (default $HVIBE_MIN_WIDTH, else 80) auto-picks N when omitted:
208	  N = clamp(term_width / min-width, 1, 6)
209	$HVIBE_LAUNCH_STAGGER (seconds, default 0.25) delays each pane launch.
210	
211	Examples:
212	  hvibe                                       # auto N × claude
213	  hvibe 3 codex                               # 3× codex
214	  hvibe --agents claude,codex,opencode        # 3 panes, mixed
215	  hvibe --tab-per-agent --agents claude,codex # one tab each
216	  hvibe --no-specstory 2 claude               # raw claude
217	EOF
218	                return 0 ;;

48:## cwd & workspace-naming model
50:herdr tracks cwd differently from tmux, which trips up two common expectations (all verified via `herdr pane list`):
52:- **Every pane has two cwds.** `cwd` = the shell's *startup* directory (fixed at spawn); `foreground_cwd` = the *live* cwd, tracked via **OSC 7** shell integration. A `cd` in the shell updates `foreground_cwd`; the startup `cwd` never changes.
53:- **`cd` inside a child process / subshell doesn't propagate.** Because tracking is OSC 7-based, a `cd` in a subshell that doesn't re-emit OSC 7 — e.g. `chezmoi cd`, which spawns a *new* shell in the source dir — is invisible to herdr. `foreground_cwd` stays put, so the space's git-repo detection and the `prefix+G` lazygit location don't follow the subshell. This is inherent to OSC 7, **not** a herdr bug — expected behavior.
54:- **New tabs follow the focused pane's live cwd (herdr ≥0.7.x).** With `new_cwd = "follow"` (below), a *new tab* inherits the focused pane's live cwd — same as a *split*. herdr [issue #912](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/issues/912) changed `follow` so tabs behave like splits; the older "new tab opens at the workspace root (often `$HOME`)" was treated as a bug and removed. There is **no `new_cwd` value** (and no workspace-level cwd — `herdr workspace get` exposes none) that opens a new tab at the workspace root; for that use **`prefix+C`** (below).
55:- **The workspace ("space") label auto-follows the root/primary pane's live cwd basename** (e.g. → `chezmoi`, `trading-journal`). `cd` in **tab 1** renames the space; `cd` in other tabs does not. No config knob controls this.
57:**`new_cwd` values** (`[terminal]`) — the CWD policy for new panes/tabs/workspaces when no explicit `--cwd` is given:
61:| `follow` (default) | inherit the **source** pane — for both a split *and* a new tab, the focused pane's live cwd (herdr ≥0.7.x) |
66:**No `new_cwd` value opens a new tab at the workspace ("space") root** — `follow` now tracks the focused pane, and herdr exposes no workspace-level cwd field. This repo ships that behavior as a keybind: **`prefix+C`** → `~/.config/herdr/new-tab-at-space-root.sh` (`dot_config/herdr/executable_new-tab-at-space-root.sh`), which derives the space root — the lowest-numbered tab's pane live cwd, i.e. what herdr uses for the space label — and runs `herdr tab create --workspace <wid> --cwd <root> --focus`. Native `prefix+c` **and the mouse "+" button** keep the follow-focused-pane behavior; a keybind cannot intercept the mouse button.
89:| File-path picker (`prefix+p`; extrakto `prefix+Tab` on tmux) | **Custom command pane + helper** | `prefix+p` → `path-pick.sh` — two-tier (exists-under-cwd first) → `x copy` |
97:Prefix is `ctrl+b` (same as tmux). Built-in actions can only be *rebound* (herdr's action set is fixed); everything else is a `[[keys.command]]` custom command. Custom commands receive `$HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`, `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID`, `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD` and run from the focused pane's cwd.
133:| `` prefix + p `` | **copy a file path** from the pane — two-tier fzf (paths that exist under the pane cwd on top), copies the resolved absolute path (`x copy`) | command pane |
135:| `prefix + E` | **run any command** in the pane's cwd — fzf-pick from history or type it; the popup closes itself when the command exits ([details](#run-any-command)) | command **popup** |
176:- **The plain-open pair (`hhere` / `hroot`)** fills the gap where every other herdr entry point forces a git repo + a full agent layout. With tmux, `tmux new-session` lands you in `$PWD` directly; herdr adds a Workspace layer, so without these you'd launch herdr, create a space (which opens at `$HOME` per `new_cwd`), then `cd` by hand. `hhere` does the one-shot: `herdr workspace create --cwd "$PWD"` → focus → attach if outside. No git requirement; the optional command runs **raw** (no specstory/on-exit wrapping — that stays with `hcode`/`hvibe`). `hhere -h` / `hroot -h` for flags. **Label caveat**: herdr auto-relabels a workspace to its root pane's *live* cwd basename after a `cd` in tab 1 (see the **cwd & workspace-naming model** section above), so the idempotent-focus is best-effort — a drifted label makes a re-run open a fresh workspace.
208:- `herdr-sesh` (`dot_config/television/cable/herdr-sesh.toml`) — lists herdr sessions/workspaces + zoxide dirs; Enter dispatches `herdr session attach` / `herdr workspace focus` / `herdr workspace create --cwd` instead of `sesh connect` / `tmux switch-client`.
326:`prefix + G` proves the shape — a transient pane that runs something and vanishes when it exits — but its command is hardcoded. `prefix + E` is the generalisation: **fzf-pick a command from shell history (or just type a new one), it runs in the focused pane's cwd, and the popup closes itself on exit.** Helper: `~/.config/herdr/run-command.sh` = [`dot_config/herdr/executable_run-command.sh`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_config/herdr/executable_run-command.sh).
346:| **cwd** | `--cwd` → `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD` → `herdr pane get` `foreground_cwd` → `$PWD`. Preferring the env var means it still works when the CLI is protocol-mismatched with a stale server |
361:| `process` | `prefix+P` | *Copy pane: process info* | foreground processes — `cmdline` + `pid` + `cwd` (from `herdr pane process-info`) |
396:| Existence check (the noise-killer) | Each candidate is resolved against the pane cwd (`$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD`, else `herdr pane get` `foreground_cwd`, else process-info cwd) and `test -e`'d |
```
</details></tool-use>

# Resolve the git repo root, or return non-zero if not in a repo.
function _sesh_git_root() {

}

# Sanitize a string for use as a tmux session name.
# tmux forbids `.` and `:` in session names; we also strip whitespace.
function _sesh_sanitize() {

# Switch to or attach to a tmux session named $1 (creating it at $2 if needed).
# Inside tmux: `switch-client`. Outside tmux: `attach-session`.
function _sesh_attach_or_switch() {
    local session="$1"
    if [ -n "$TMUX" ]; then
        tmux switch-client -t "$session"
    else
        tmux attach-session -t "$session"
    fi
}

# Create (or no-op if exists) a detached tmux session at the given path.
# Returns 0 if the session already existed, 1 if newly created. (Caller uses
# this to decide whether to apply layout setup or just attach.)

            -*)           echo "sesh-here: unknown flag $1" >&2; return 1 ;;

    if [ -n "$cmd" ]; then
        sesh connect --command "$cmd" "$target"
    else
        # Bypass sesh's default_session.startup_command (nvim) for a plain
        # shell. We create the session via tmux directly, then attach. This
        # also means the wildcard startup_command (project layout) is
        # bypassed — `shere` is intentionally lightweight; use `scode`,
        # `svibe`, or `sesh connect <path>` for layouts.
        local session
        session=$(_sesh_sanitize "$(basename "$target")")
        _sesh_ensure_session "$session" "$target"
        _sesh_attach_or_switch "$session"
    fi
}

# Same smart argument handling as sesh-here.

function sesh-root() {
    local cmd="" root
    while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
        case "$1" in

- `herdr session attach NAME` · `herdr session stop NAME` · `herdr session delete NAME` (`default` is a valid `NAME` for stop).

**Targeting a session from the CLI subcommands**: there is **no `--session`/`--socket` flag** on `workspace`/`tab`/`pane`/`agent`. The only lever is the **`HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`** env var — set it to a session's `socket_path` and every subcommand routes there. Inside a herdr pane it is already exported to the current session's socket, so scripts run *inside* herdr target the current session for free. This is exactly how `hvibe --session NAME` works (see below).

## cwd & workspace-naming model

herdr tracks cwd differently from tmux, which trips up two common expectations (all verified via `herdr pane list`):

- **Every pane has two cwds.** `cwd` = the shell's *startup* directory (fixed at spawn); `foreground_cwd` = the *live* cwd, tracked via **OSC 7** shell integration. A `cd` in the shell updates `foreground_cwd`; the startup `cwd` never changes.
- **`cd` inside a child process / subshell doesn't propagate.** Because tracking is OSC 7-based, a `cd` in a subshell that doesn't re-emit OSC 7 — e.g. `chezmoi cd`, which spawns a *new* shell in the source dir — is invisible to herdr. `foreground_cwd` stays put, so the space's git-repo detection and the `prefix+G` lazygit location don't follow the subshell. This is inherent to OSC 7, **not** a herdr bug — expected behavior.
- **New tabs follow the focused pane's live cwd (herdr ≥0.7.x).** With `new_cwd = "follow"` (below), a *new tab* inherits the focused pane's live cwd — same as a *split*. herdr [issue #912](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/issues/912) changed `follow` so tabs behave like splits; the older "new tab opens at the workspace root (often `$HOME`)" was treated as a bug and removed. There is **no `new_cwd` value** (and no workspace-level cwd — `herdr workspace get` exposes none) that opens a new tab at the workspace root; for that use **`prefix+C`** (below).
- **The workspace ("space") label auto-follows the root/primary pane's live cwd basename** (e.g. → `chezmoi`, `trading-journal`). `cd` in **tab 1** renames the space; `cd` in other tabs does not. No config knob controls this.

**`new_cwd` values** (`[terminal]`) — the CWD policy for new panes/tabs/workspaces when no explicit `--cwd` is given:

| value | meaning |
|---|---|
| `follow` (default) | inherit the **source** pane — for both a split *and* a new tab, the focused pane's live cwd (herdr ≥0.7.x) |
| `home` | `$HOME` |
| `current` | herdr's **own process** directory (NOT the focused pane) |
| `"~/path"` | a fixed path |

**No `new_cwd` value opens a new tab at the workspace ("space") root** — `follow` now tracks the focused pane, and herdr exposes no workspace-level cwd field. This repo ships that behavior as a keybind: **`prefix+C`** → `~/.config/herdr/new-tab-at-space-root.sh` (`dot_config/herdr/executable_new-tab-at-space-root.sh`), which derives the space root — the lowest-numbered tab's pane live cwd, i.e. what herdr uses for the space label — and runs `herdr tab create --workspace <wid> --cwd <root> --focus`. Native `prefix+c` **and the mouse "+" button** keep the follow-focused-pane behavior; a keybind cannot intercept the mouse button.

```toml
[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+C"
======== ZH ========
herdr 的階層是 **Session → Workspace → Tab → Pane**——比 tmux（Session → Window → Pane）多一層。「Workspace」是專案層級的容器；「Tab」把多個 pane 分組。CLI（`herdr session|workspace|tab|pane|agent …`，大多支援 `--json`）是取代 `tmux switch-client` / `list-sessions` 等指令的腳本介面。

跟 tmux 最關鍵的差異：單一 herdr **server 會託管多個具名 session (named sessions)**，每個 session 各自是一棵持久化的樹、各自有自己的 socket。最上層的 **Session** 這一層，比較接近「多個 tmux server / socket」，而不是 tmux 的 session——你在 tmux 會叫做 session 的東西（`vibe/<repo>`）在 herdr 對應的是 **Workspace**，而不是 herdr Session。

### 具名 session (Named sessions) {#named-sessions}

- `herdr` —— 啟動或 attach **default** session（socket `~/.config/herdr/herdr.sock`）。
- `herdr --session NAME` —— 啟動/attach 一個**具名** session（socket `~/.config/herdr/sessions/<NAME>/herdr.sock`）。
- `herdr session list [--json]` —— 列出所有 session 及其 `running` + `socket_path`。**`--json` 的 `socket_path` 才是權威值**——純文字表格印出的是 `herdr.socket`，但真正的 socket 是 `herdr.sock`。
- `herdr session attach NAME` · `herdr session stop NAME` · `herdr session delete NAME`（stop 時 `default` 是合法的 `NAME`）。

**從 CLI 子指令鎖定某個 session**：`workspace`/`tab`/`pane`/`agent` **沒有 `--session`/`--socket` flag**。唯一的槓桿是 **`HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`** 這個環境變數 (env var)——把它設成某 session 的 `socket_path`，所有子指令就會導向該 session。在 herdr pane 內部它已經被 export 成當前 session 的 socket，所以*在 herdr 內*跑的腳本天生就鎖定當前 session。`hvibe --session NAME` 正是靠這個機制運作（見下文）。

## cwd 與 workspace 命名模型

herdr 追蹤 cwd 的方式跟 tmux 不同,會顛覆兩個常見預期（皆用 `herdr pane list` 驗證）:

- **每個 pane 有兩個 cwd。** `cwd` = shell 的*啟動*目錄（spawn 時固定）;`foreground_cwd` = *即時* cwd,透過 **OSC 7** shell 整合追蹤。shell 裡 `cd` 會更新 `foreground_cwd`;啟動 `cwd` 永不變。
- **子行程 / 子 shell 裡的 `cd` 不會傳上來。** 因為追蹤是 OSC 7-based,一個沒有再送 OSC 7 的子 shell 裡的 `cd`——例如 `chezmoi cd`,它會在 source 目錄 spawn 一個*新*shell——對 herdr 是隱形的。`foreground_cwd` 不動,所以 space 的 git-repo 偵測與 `prefix+G` lazygit 位置都不跟著子 shell 走。這是 OSC 7 的固有特性,**不是** herdr bug——預期行為。
- **新 tab 跟隨聚焦 pane 的即時 cwd（herdr ≥0.7.x）。** 用 `new_cwd = "follow"`（見下）時,*新 tab* 繼承聚焦 pane 的即時 cwd——跟 *split* 一樣。herdr [issue #912](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/issues/912) 改了 `follow`,讓 tab 跟 split 行為一致;舊的「新 tab 開在 workspace 根（通常 `$HOME`）」被當成 bug 移除了。**沒有任何 `new_cwd` 值**（也沒有 workspace 層級的 cwd——`herdr workspace get` 完全沒有 cwd 欄位）能讓新 tab 開在 workspace 根;要那樣請用下方的 **`prefix+C`**。
- **workspace（space）label 自動跟隨 root/primary pane 的即時 cwd basename**（例如 → `chezmoi`、`trading-journal`）。在 **tab 1** 裡 `cd` 會改 space 名;在其他 tab 裡 `cd` 不會。沒有 config 旋鈕控制這個。

**`new_cwd` 值**（`[terminal]`）—— 沒給明確 `--cwd` 時,新 pane/tab/workspace 的 CWD 政策:

| 值 | 意義 |
```

# Pitfalls

Past traps we've stepped on. Symptoms-first knowledge base — the goal is that
when a problem recurs (on a new machine, after an upgrade, with a new tool
combo), grepping the symptom here lands you on the root cause and workaround
in seconds, instead of re-debugging from scratch.

This folder is `chezmoi`-ignored (see `.chezmoiignore.tmpl` → `pitfalls/**`); it
is repo metadata for maintainers, not user-facing config to deploy.

## Pitfalls vs the rest

This repo has four sibling surfaces with overlapping shapes; pick the right one:

| Surface | Time direction | Question it answers | Access pattern |
|---|---|---|---|
| `docs/tools/<tool>.md` | Present | "How does this tool work / how do I configure it?" | Read top to bottom |
| `docs/this_repo/<topic>.md` | Present | "Why did we architect it this way?" | Read top to bottom |
| `pitfalls/<slug>.md` | **Past** | **"I see error X — has this happened before?"** | **Grep symptoms** |
| `backlog/<slug>.md` | Future | "We thought about doing Y — what was the analysis?" | Index in `TODO.md` |
| `AGENTS.md` Hard invariants | Present | "What rules MUST agents follow?" | Read top to bottom |

A pitfall **graduates** to a Hard invariant in `AGENTS.md` when the trap is
serious enough that you can't rely on memory or grep — typically when (a) it
recurs across machines, (b) it silently corrupts state, or (c) the workaround
is non-obvious and easy to undo by accident. When graduating, leave a
`pitfalls/<slug>.md` as historical record and link to it from the invariant.

## When to add a pitfall doc

Add a `pitfalls/<slug>.md` when you've spent more than ~15 minutes on something
where the answer wasn't googleable, AND any of:

- The symptom is non-obvious from the root cause (`SSH_CONNECTION` cleared
  silently → hostname module disappears, no error)
- The fix is "do nothing different but in a specific order" (sentinel writes
  must come after `wait $pid` for fleet-apply, etc.)
- The same trap could be hit by a new agent / new machine / new contributor
- An upstream bug exists with no ETA — workaround needs to outlive memory
- A specific tool version is required (or forbidden) and the failure mode at

```text
# herdr CLI dies with `protocol_mismatch` after `brew upgrade herdr` — and Homebrew installs cannot live-handoff

## Symptoms

Right after `brew upgrade herdr` on macOS, **every** `herdr` CLI call fails while the
UI you are sitting in keeps working perfectly:

```console
$ herdr workspace list
{"id":"cli:workspace:list","error":{"code":"protocol_mismatch",
 "message":"client protocol 17 is newer than server protocol 16; restart the Herdr server
 before using this command. Stop the old server to use the new version.\nStopping exits pane
 processes.\nRun `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH=/Users/you/.config/herdr/herdr.sock herdr server stop`,
 then restart Herdr with the same socket override."}}
```

Note the exit code is **0** — the error is in the JSON body, not the process status, so
naive `cmd || fallback` wrappers do not notice.

```console
$ herdr status
client:
  version: 0.7.5
  protocol: 17
server:
  status: running
  version: 0.7.2
  protocol: 16
  compatible: no
update:
  restart_needed: yes
```

Downstream, in this repo, that means the following silently stop working (usually as an
**empty picker** rather than an error, because the tv channels pipe through `jq` and
swallow stderr with `2>/dev/null`):

- `prefix + T` → `tv herdr-sesh`, `prefix + a` → `tv herdr-agent-panes`, `prefix + i` → `tv herdr-review`
- `hvibe` / `hcode` / `hhere` / `hroot` (`dot_config/shell/24_herdr.sh`)
- every `[[keys.command]]` helper that calls the CLI: `review-mark.sh`, `pane-copy.sh`,
  `path-pick.sh`, `url-pick.sh`, `new-tab-at-space-root.sh`

The herdr TUI itself is unaffected — the running server and its attached client are both
still the old binary, talking the old protocol to each other.

=== index? ===

Silent removal: not listed as a breaking change upstream |
135:| [`herdr-brew-upgrade-strands-running-server`](herdr-brew-upgrade-strands-running-server.md) | after `brew upgrade herdr` every `herdr` CLI call returns `{"error":{"code":"protocol_mismatch"}}` (`client protocol 17 is newer than server protocol 16`) while the TUI works fine; **exit code still 0**; `tv herdr-sesh` / `herdr-agent-panes` / `herdr-review` open empty; `hvibe`/`hcode` and the `prefix+m/p/u/P/D/V/S` helpers do nothing; `herdr status` shows `compatible: no` + `restart_needed: yes`; `herdr --version` misleadingly reports the NEW version | by design (fail-closed protocol gate) — and `herdr update --handoff` is **disabled on Homebrew/mise/Nix installs**, so macOS has no pane-preserving path; wait for a restart point, `herdr server stop` + reattach (topology + agent sessions restore, processes die), or `brew pin herdr` |
136:| [`herdr-update-handoff-refuses-inside-pane`](herdr-update-handoff-refuses-inside-pane.md) | `herdr update --handoff` exits immediately with `update failed: run herdr update outside herdr after detaching from the session`, before any `checking stable channel` line; the same command works from another terminal seconds later; a coding agent shelling out can never fix it, because the guard reads `HERDR_ENV` and not the invocation | by design (the handoff replaces the server that owns your pane) — detach `prefix+q` → update from a plain terminal → reattach with bare `herdr`; the handoff does preserve running panes. `just upgrade-herdr` now skips-with-instructions rather than failing |

```md
# `hhere -p ../sibling` ignores the path and opens the workspace at `~`

## Symptoms

From a repo, point `hhere` at a sibling directory with a **relative** path:

\```console
Pueue-Raycast-Extension on  main
❯ hhere -p ../Agent-Deck-Raycast-Extension
\```

The command **succeeds** — exit 0, nothing on stderr, no herdr error JSON — and a
workspace is created. But the new space's shell is sitting in `$HOME`, not in
`../Agent-Deck-Raycast-Extension`. Confirm with:

\```console
$ herdr pane list --workspace w1E | jq -r '.result.panes[].cwd'
/Users/david
\```

Two details that make this hard to spot:

- **Absolute paths work fine.** `hhere -p ~/Documents/Program/Foo` (the shell
  expands `~` before `hhere` ever sees it) lands correctly, so the flag looks
  like it works — only the relative form is broken.
- **The workspace label is still right.** The label comes from `basename` in the
  shell function, so the space is *named* `Agent-Deck-Raycast-Extension` while
  its pane is in `~`. herdr only auto-relabels to the live cwd basename after a
  `cd` in tab 1, so nothing renames the space to `~` to give the game away.

The same applied to `hcode -p ../foo` / `hvibe -p ../foo`, but there the miss
surfaced as the misleading error `not inside a git repo` instead.

## Root cause

**`herdr workspace create --cwd` is resolved by the herdr *server*, not by the
calling shell.** The server's own working directory is whatever directory
`herdr server` happened to be launched from — for a server started from this
repo, `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi`:

\```console
$ lsof -a -p "$(pgrep -f 'herdr server')" -d cwd | tail -1
herdr  1576 david  cwd  DIR  1,5  2528  24013827  /Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi
\```

So the relative path is joined to *that*, not to your `$PWD`. Proof — from
`/tmp/hh-test/alpha`, both of these ignore `$PWD` completely:

\```console
$ cd /tmp/hh-test/alpha
$ herdr workspace create --cwd ./docs --label T --no-focus | jq -r '.result.root_pane.cwd'
/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/docs      # ← server cwd + ./docs

$ herdr workspace create --cwd ../bravo --label T2 --no-focus | jq -r '.result.root_pane.cwd'
/Users/david                                # ← miss → SILENT fallback to $HOME
\```

The second line is the whole bug: when the server-side join misses, herdr does
**not** error — it falls back to `$HOME` and returns `{"result":{"type":"ok"}}`.

**tmux does not behave this way**, which is why the sesh originals
(`shere` / `scode` / `svibe`) never needed a guard and the herdr ports looked
like faithful analogs. tmux resolves `new-session -c` **client-side**:

\```console
$ cd /tmp/tmux-rel/alpha
$ tmux new-session -d -s T -c ../bravo
$ tmux display-message -p -t T '#{pane_current_path}'
/private/tmp/tmux-rel/bravo                 # ← correct, despite the tmux server
                                            #   also living in .../chezmoi
\```

## Fix

Absolutize `-p/--path` **in the calling shell**, before it reaches herdr —
`dot_config/shell/24_herdr.sh` → `_herdr_abs_dir`, used by `hhere`, `hcode`,
and `hvibe`:

\```bash
function _herdr_abs_dir() {
    local abs
    abs=$(CDPATH=''; cd -- "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 && pwd -P)
    if [ -z "$abs" ]; then
        echo "${2:-herdr}: --path is not a directory: $1" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    printf '%s\n' "$abs"
}
\```

- `CDPATH=''` — without it, a `CDPATH` hit can retarget the `cd` to a *different*
  directory of the same name **and** echo the resolved path into the capture,
  giving a two-line `$target`. (Same idiom already used in
  `dot_config/herdr/executable_path-pick.sh`.) Path arguments should not honour
  `CDPATH`; `-p bravo` now means `./bravo`, always.
- `--` — a target beginning with `-` is a path, not a `cd` flag.
- `>/dev/null` — belt-and-braces against the same echo.
- `pwd -P` — canonicalize symlinks, matching what `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`
  returns for the `hcode`/`hvibe` paths.
- **Returning 1 on a non-directory is the point.** Previously a typo'd `-p` was
  indistinguishable from success; now `hhere -p ../typo` says
  `hhere: --path is not a directory: ../typo` instead of silently opening `~`,
  and `hcode -p ../typo` no longer misreports it as `not inside a git repo`.

`hroot` needs nothing — it derives its path from `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`
(absolute) and passes it through `hhere`.

## Generalisable rule

**Any path handed to a daemon over a socket must be absolutized by the client.**
The server has its own cwd and no idea where you are. This applies to every
`--cwd` in `24_herdr.sh` and to future herdr CLI surfaces
(`tab create --cwd`, `pane split --cwd`) — those are currently safe only because
they are fed `$repo_root` from `git rev-parse`, which is already absolute. If a
new call site ever gets a user-supplied path, route it through `_herdr_abs_dir`.

The `--cwd` consumers that are *not* affected, and why:

| Call site | Path source | Safe because |
|---|---|---|
| `24_herdr.sh` `hvibe`/`hcode` `workspace create` / `pane split` / `_herdr_tool_tab` | `_sesh_git_root` | `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` is absolute |
| `dot_config/herdr/executable_new-tab-at-space-root.sh` | `herdr pane get` → `foreground_cwd` | herdr reports absolute paths |
| `dot_config/television/cable/herdr-sesh.toml` → `actions.open` | zoxide | `zoxide query -l` emits absolute paths |

## Related

- [`docs/tools/herdr.md`](../docs/tools/herdr.md) § cwd & workspace-naming model
- `dot_config/shell/22_sesh.sh` — the tmux originals, unaffected (client-side `-c`)

```

hhere — open a plain herdr workspace here + attach (herdr analog of shere)

Usage: hhere [--path DIR] [--command CMD] [--no-attach] [--session NAME] [CMD...]

_**Agent (claude-opus-5 2026-07-27 05:09:16Z)**_

修好了，而且是真的 bug — 我先重現再修的。

## 根因

`herdr workspace create --cwd` 的相對路徑是**由 herdr server 解析的，不是由你的 shell**。Server 的 cwd 是它當初被啟動的目錄：

```console
$ lsof -a -p "$(pgrep -f 'herdr server')" -d cwd | tail -1
herdr 1576 david cwd DIR ... /Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi
```

所以 `hhere -p ../Agent-Deck-Raycast-Extension` 送出去的是字面上的 `../Agent-Deck-...`，server 把它接在自己的啟動目錄後面。實測（從 `/tmp/hh-test/alpha` 執行）：

```console
$ herdr workspace create --cwd ./docs   → cwd = /Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/docs   # server cwd + 相對路徑
$ herdr workspace create --cwd ../bravo → cwd = /Users/david                             # 接不到 → 靜默退回 $HOME
```

第二行就是你看到的症狀：**沒有 error、exit 0、回傳 `{"result":{"type":"ok"}}`**，pane 直接開在 `~`。

兩個讓它難以察覺的地方：絕對路徑（`-p ~/foo`，`~` 由 shell 展開）完全正常，所以 flag 看起來是好的；而且 workspace 的 label 是 shell 這邊用 `basename` 算的，所以 space 名字還是對的 `Agent-Deck-Raycast-Extension`，只有 pane 在 `~`。

順帶確認了 tmux **不是**這樣 —— `tmux new-session -c ../bravo` 是 client 端解析，結果正確。這就是為什麼 `shere`/`scode`/`svibe` 原版從來不需要防護，移植到 herdr 時這個差異被漏掉了。

## 修法

`dot_config/shell/24_herdr.sh` 新增 `_herdr_abs_dir`，在**呼叫端 shell** 就把 `-p` 絕對化，`hhere` / `hcode` / `hvibe` 三個都接上去：

```bash
abs=$(CDPATH=''; cd -- "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 && pwd -P)
```

`CDPATH=''` 是為了避免 CDPATH 命中時 `cd` 跑去別的同名目錄、又把路徑 echo 進 capture 變成兩行；路徑參數本來就不該吃 CDPATH。目錄不存在改成**硬錯誤**，不再靜默開 `$HOME`：

```console
$ hhere -p ../typo
hhere: --path is not a directory: ../typo      # 以前：exit 0，開在 ~
$ hcode -p ../typo
hcode: --path is not a directory: ../typo      # 以前誤報 "not inside a git repo"
```

`hroot` 不用改（路徑來自 `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`，本來就是絕對的）。

## 驗證

bash / zsh 都跑過 `-n`、pre-commit 全過，並實際端到端測試（建 workspace → 查 `herdr pane list` → 關掉）：

- `hhere -p ../ZZLIVE-bravo` → `cwd=/private/tmp/hh-live/ZZLIVE-bravo` ✓（修前會是 `/Users/david`）
- `hcode -p ../ZZLIVE-repo`（relative + git repo）→ 三個 pane 全部落在正確路徑 ✓
- 相對 / `.` / `..` / 尾斜線 / 檔案而非目錄 / 不存在 / CDPATH 命中，bash 與 zsh 行為一致 ✓

另外同步更新了 repo contract 要求的鏡像：`pitfalls/hhere-p-relative-path-opens-workspace-at-home.md`（含 README 索引列）、`docs/tools/herdr.md` 的 cwd 模型與 hhere 段落 + `.zh-TW` 鏡像、`docs/shells/aliases.md` 的 `hhere` 那列。`mkdocs build` 沒有新增 warning（只有既有的 baseline INFO）。

已經 `chezmoi apply` 部署了，但**現有的 shell 還握著舊的 function** — 開新 shell 或 `source ~/.config/shell/24_herdr.sh` 才會生效。尚未 commit，等你確認。

launch directory, not by the calling shell — and on a miss herdr falls back to
$HOME and still returns `{"result":{"type":"ok"}}`. So only the relative form
broke (absolute `-p ~/foo` is shell-expanded and worked), and the space kept
the correct label — that is computed shell-side from basename — while its pane
sat in $HOME, so nothing renamed it to `~` to give the game away. hcode/hvibe
hit the same miss but misreported it as `not inside a git repo`.

tmux is the opposite: `new-session -c ../foo` is client-resolved. That is why
the sesh originals (shere/scode/svibe) never needed a guard, and why the herdr
ports inherited the gap unnoticed.

New `_herdr_abs_dir` canonicalizes `-p` in the calling shell for all three
entry points and hard-errors on a non-directory instead of silently opening
$HOME. `CDPATH=''` keeps a CDPATH hit from retargeting the cd or echoing the
resolved dir into the capture; path arguments should not honour CDPATH.
`hroot` needs nothing — its path comes from `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`.

Verified end-to-end against a live server: relative / `.` / `..` /
trailing-slash / missing / file-not-dir / CDPATH-hit, in both bash and zsh.
